summary: This bill requires that premiums paid for auto, home/renter, and flood insurance policies be deducted from an individual's income and resources when determining eligibility for benefits or assistance under any federal program or federally funded state or local program.

scores.thoughts: The bill mandates deducting premiums for auto, homeowner/renter, and flood insurance from countable income/resources when determining eligibility for any federal means-tested benefits or federally funded state/local programs. This change would increase the number of eligible recipients and/or benefit amounts, directly resulting in higher federal outlays on safety-net programs.
The legislation contains no provisions altering tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue collection mechanisms.

While health-related insurance is mentioned in passing, the bill addresses only the treatment of premiums in eligibility calculations for existing benefit programs and does not modify healthcare coverage, delivery, or financing structures.
No provisions relate to firearms regulation, ownership, or rights.
No provisions address immigration status, pathways, enforcement, or border policy.
No provisions address reproductive healthcare access or restrictions.
No provisions affect military or defense budgets or policy.

Flood insurance is included among the covered policies, but the bill merely adjusts how those premiums factor into benefit eligibility; it neither expands nor limits environmental regulations or protections.

By lowering countable income for eligibility determinations across all federal means-tested programs, the bill expands access to welfare, housing, nutrition, and similar assistance, directly broadening the social safety net.
No provisions address schools, student aid, or education policy.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or related programs.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or justice-system reforms.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
The eligibility expansion would increase mandatory spending and therefore deficits, but the bill itself does not contain debt-reduction measures or explicit deficit policy.
No provisions address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions address foreign assistance or international aid.
No provisions address voting access, election administration, or voter ID.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No provisions address worker protections, union rights, or employer obligations.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
